universal_lens: The mapping from session-reference peak-velocity-decline thresholds to working-set repetition volumes constitutes a non-linear operator over the metabolic fatigue manifold. Volitional failure represents an asymptotic boundary condition where mechanical power output collapses, yielding distinct but isomorphic strength adaptations across sub-maximal and maximal exposure domains.
gsi_mapping: GSI models the observed repetition volumes as a latent variable governed by a Bayesian hierarchical structure. The posterior distribution of strength gains remains highly collinear between the 40% velocity decline and failure states, allowing conformal prediction intervals to safely truncate training volume while maintaining statistical coverage for primary force outcomes.

reasoning_traces.think:
The mathematical core of this study lies in the non-linear mapping between a kinematic threshold (peak-velocity-decline) and the resulting volumetric integral (repetition count). By fixing the external load at 30% 1RM under BFR, the authors isolate the set-termination strategy as the primary independent variable. The derivation shows that a 40% decline in peak velocity yields a repetition volume that sits precisely on the inflection point of the strength-adaptation curve. Beyond this point, extending the set to volitional failure (FAIL) drastically increases the volumetric integral and perceived exertion (RPE), yet the marginal gain in primary strength outcomes (1RM, IMTP) approaches zero. This establishes a mathematical redundancy between the 40% decline and failure states regarding maximal force production. However, when projecting these states onto the secondary power-manifold (jump metrics), the isomorphism breaks. The excessive fatigue accumulated in the FAIL state introduces a negative bias into the rate-of-force-development (RFD) adaptations, suppressing countermovement-jump (CMJ) and squat-jump (SJ) improvements compared to the truncated 40% and 10% conditions. Thus, the operators define a multi-dimensional optimization landscape where minimizing volume via velocity tracking preserves power-output capabilities without sacrificing absolute strength.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a decision-theory perspective, the athlete acts as an agent balancing immediate discomfort against long-term performance gains. The FAIL strategy forces the agent into a high-cost, high-discomfort regime driven by a psychological bias toward exhaustive effort. Conversely, the velocity-decline operators provide an objective, externalized stopping rule, allowing the agent to achieve equivalent strength adaptations with significantly reduced cognitive and physical strain, optimizing the subjective utility function of the training session.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: To prevent leakage between the strength and power layers, we must veto any programming logic that assumes linear transferability of fatigue. If an athlete prioritizes maximal strength (primary outcomes), the system can safely substitute FAIL with VL40%. However, if explosive power (secondary outcomes) is the dominant objective, the system must veto the FAIL state entirely, enforcing stricter velocity-decline thresholds (e.g., VL10%) to preserve neuromuscular elasticity and avoid catabolic interference with fast-twitch fiber recruitment.
